title: Classification-aware certificate: does a per-class score-margin model, built from the Gram spectrum and label projections alone, predict M116's measured accuracy crossing? (the M121 fix)

source.features: reuses M116's sealed feature memmaps (data_cache_root()/v16/m116/f_train.npy 138000x12288 float32; dense_train.npy 138000x768 float32); no re-encoding, no training
source.m116_reference: logs/results/v16/m116_scale/evidence.json (measured Q(n); sparse overtakes dense between n=27600 and n=55200)

theory.formula: Canatar-Bordelon-Pehlevan 2006.13198 modal machinery (as in M121) applied PER CLASS, then a Gaussian score-margin model. Modal objects from the full-M standardised Gram: vals_k (raw eigenvalues), a_rho,c = v_rho^T (F_std^T y_c) (345-dim label projections per mode), kappa(P) and E_rho(P) = (1/(1-gamma)) kappa^2/(kappa + P*eta)^2 from the M121 fixed point. Per ladder point P: S_cc'(P) = sum_rho a_rho,c a_rho,c' / (vals_k + kappa(P)); Sigma_cc'(P) = sum_rho E_rho(P) a_rho,c a_rho,c' / vals_k (Canatar's modal error applied per class and pairwise - the per-class learnable score VARIANCE, decaying as P grows). Score model for a class-c test point: f ~ N(mu^(c)(P), Sigma(P)) with mu^(c)_c'(P) = S_cc'(P) / n_c (class-conditional modal mean estimated by the train average, exchangeability). Predicted accuracy(P) = (1/C) sum_c P(f_c > max_{c'!=c} f_c'), Monte Carlo over the Gaussian.
theory.disclosure: first-principles Gaussian margin approximation: (i) class-conditional modal means = train-class averages (exchangeability); (ii) E[b_rho^2] = 1 for standardised features (isotropic test-input covariance); (iii) joint score vector Gaussian. The covariance carries the P-dependence (E_rho -> 0 as P grows, so predicted accuracy rises); the mean carries the class-alignment structure (S/(vals+kappa)). The gate is the predicted CROSSING (shape-level), never absolute accuracy. Target power in kernel-null modes contributes ~0 to S and Sigma (a_rho ~ 0 there; no division by vals that explodes), reported as a per-class diagnostic, not gated.
theory.eigenvalues: eta_rho = eigenvalues of (1/M) F_std^T F_std, M = 138000 train rows, per-dim mean/unit-variance from train (the M116 RidgeAccumulator convention); kept modes as M121 (vals > max*1e-10)
theory.ridge_mapping: lambda = penalty = 1.0 (the program's closed-form ridge), kappa(P) self-consistently as in M121

gate.predicted_crossing: smallest ladder P where predicted sparse accuracy(P) > dense accuracy(P); PASS if within a factor [1/3, 3] of the measured M116 crossing midpoint (41400)
gate.gap_direction_at_nmax: predicted sparse accuracy(n_max) > dense accuracy(n_max) (matches M116's measured 0.2153 > 0.1972)
gate.registered_fallback: if the margin certificate still fails to predict the crossing, the certificate is CLOSED as a prediction tool and kept as an explanatory diagnostic only (per v19 section 5.2)
